title: CommonJS and ES modules
idea: A module is a file with its own private scope that shares only what it exports, using either CommonJS or ES module syntax.

analogy.text: A workshop with a service hatch. Tools and scraps stay inside; only what you pass through the hatch (the exports) reaches the next workshop.
analogy.breaks: Importers receive the same exported objects, not copies.

points: Each file is a module: its variables stay private unless it exports them.
CommonJS uses `require` and `module.exports`; ES modules use `import` and `export`.
`.cjs` is CommonJS and `.mjs` is ES modules; `.js` follows `package.json`, covered next.
Node runs each module once and caches it by its full file path.

steps.caption: A file asks for a module: `require('./math.cjs')` or `import … from './math.cjs'`. Node must find it first.
Resolve: Node turns `./math.cjs` into a full file path. That path is the module's identity.
Cache: has this path been loaded before? Not yet, so Node loads the file.
Run: Node executes `math.cjs` once, top to bottom. Its `console.log` fires now.
The file ends. What it assigned to `module.exports` is the result; its other variables stay private.
The cache now holds the module's exports under its path, ready for the next request.
The caller gets the exports and carries on. The first load is done.
Later, a second file in this folder asks for `./math.cjs`.
Resolve produces the same full path as before.
Cache: this path is already stored. A hit, so Node skips the Run stage.
Node returns the stored exports. The file does not run again, so nothing new prints.
Both files now share one exports object, and the module ran once.

code.title: The module
code.caption: A CommonJS module. `module.exports` is what other files receive; `secret` stays private.

code.title: CommonJS importer
code.caption: `require` runs `math.cjs` at the moment it is called, in the middle of this file.

code.title: ES module importer
code.caption: The same file as an ES module. Compare the order of the first two output lines with `main.cjs`.

walk.text: `import` pulls in `add`. ES modules can import CommonJS files such as `math.cjs`.
Imports load before the file's own code runs, so `math.cjs` prints first.
`secret` was never exported, so no such name exists here.

pitfalls: Use `import`, not `require`, in `.mjs` files; `require` is not defined there.
Write the extension in ES module imports of your own files: `./math.cjs`, not `./math`.
Keep per-request data inside functions; module-level variables are shared by every importer.

options: math: loading, math: loading, then done
quiz.why: Node caches a module by its path. The second `require` returns the stored exports, so `math.cjs` does not run again.

takeaway: Share through exports, load by path, and remember a module loads only once.
